Source: the recorded arXiv e-print hash reproduces byte for byte (362cf73f69e7a7adc58c10667cf3226004842e3384191bd2b628bc43ca1c29b1); the archive is a bare gzipped file, and it is the recorded AMZV_ZagierHoffman_arxiv_v2.tex, 4640 lines, which I read. The extraction's locator convention is unusual and it is right. The preprint leaves the introduction unnumbered, so its statements are numbered 0.k, while the published version numbers the introduction as §1 and everything shifts by one; every locator gives the preprint number with the published one in parentheses, and `source.read` says so. I verified the convention from the source: there are exactly four `\section` commands, so the introduction is indeed unnumbered, and the `theorem` counter is `[section]`-numbered with conjecture, lemma, proposition, corollary, definition, remark, example and notation all sharing it, while `theoremx` is a separate counter — which is why Theorems A and B keep their letters, as the note says. The single library item's four declarations resolve: Mathlib's Polynomial, RatFunc, LaurentSeries and Polynomial.Monic. All 31 resolve to a statement of exactly the cited kind and number. No locator error. The single finding is confirmed verbatim. The definition of the alternating multiple zeta values writes $\fs=(s_1,\dots,s_r)\in\N^n$ and $\fve=(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_r)\in(\Fq^\times)^n$ while both tuples have $r$ entries, the sum runs over $(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in A_+^r$, and $r$ is named as the depth two lines below; $n$ is not in scope there. The same objects are written with exponent $r$ when the alternating Carlitz multiple polylogarithms are introduced, which is the contrast the finding gives. `affects: nothing` is right. I verified them against the index this lane uses and they are there.
